desc:
Ecom Swift LLC provides Android app development in Kotlin: a native app designed, built and tested on real phones, then prepared for release in your own Google Play Console. You receive the full source code when we hand it over.

## What is native Android app development?

Native Android app development means writing the app in Kotlin, the language Google recommends for Android, using the platform's own tools such as Android Studio and Jetpack Compose. A native app talks directly to the phone, so it can use the camera, notifications, sensors and billing without workarounds.

We agree the screens and features in writing first. Then we build in short steps, so you see real progress on your own phone instead of waiting for one big reveal.

## Why a well-built Android app is worth the care

Your app sits on a customer's home screen every day, which is a stronger position than a web page they visit once. That position is easy to lose. An app that stalls on launch, crashes on older phones or asks for permissions without a reason is deleted in seconds, and a poor first release is hard to recover from in the store.

A proper build also protects you later. Clean structure, sensible naming and tests mean the next developer can add features without breaking what exists. You own the result, not a tangle that only its author understands.

## How build quality affects users and revenue

People judge an app in the first minute. A fast start, clear navigation and screens that respond at once tell them the product is dependable. If the app sells something, a smooth sign-in and a simple purchase step remove reasons to quit before paying.

Android adds its own tests: different screen sizes, the back gesture, dark theme and a wide range of hardware. Building for these from the start keeps ratings healthier and support requests fewer. We cannot promise downloads or sales, because marketing and demand matter too, but a sound app gives your marketing something worth sending people to.

## What a great Android build includes

- A written scope listing every screen, feature and data field before coding begins.
- Kotlin code with Jetpack Compose, organized into clear layers.
- A launcher icon and splash screen that match your brand.
- Local storage on the device, or a cloud connection when the app needs one.
- Google or email sign-in where accounts are required.
- Push notifications through Firebase, when your plan calls for them.
- Play Billing for purchases or subscriptions in the fuller packages.
- Layouts that adapt to small phones, large phones and tablets.
- Testing on several phone sizes and Android versions before every handover.
- Source code and plain handover notes that belong to you.

## How we work

We begin with a short call or written brief, then turn it into a screen list for your approval. You receive builds through a Play internal testing link, so you install updates the same way your customers will. The Basic package covers a simple app with a few screens and local data. Standard adds sign-in, a backend connection, push and preparation of your store text. Premium adds billing, tablet and foldable layouts, analytics and launch support.

When you approve the build, we prepare the release inside your own Play Console, with your developer account and your name on the listing.

## Dos and mistakes to avoid in a first Android release

**Do:**
- Describe the one thing a user should be able to do in the first minute.
- Give us examples of apps you like and apps you dislike.
- Test each build on your own phone and reply with notes.
- Prepare your privacy policy address and support email early.
- Keep your scope fixed while a build is in progress.

**Avoid:**
- Adding features mid-build without agreeing what moves.
- Asking for iPhone and Android at once if budget is tight.
- Collecting data the app does not need.
- Skipping the internal testing stage to hurry a release.
- Choosing a design that ignores the Android back gesture.

## Who this is for

This service suits a business owner who wants a customer app for orders, bookings or loyalty. It suits a founder with a clear idea who needs a working first product. It also suits a creator or service business that wants a branded tool on customers' phones instead of a website alone.

## What we need from you

Send a short brief, your logo and colors, any sketches, and the list of features you expect. You need your own Google Play developer account, which we help you set up. We never ask for your passwords. Access is given by inviting us as a user in your Play Console with limited permissions, and you can remove it any time.
